nodes.label: Q1: Do Haiku rules hold in live use?
nodes.explain: Does the new easy-tier rubric (Haiku only for mechanical work with a cheap check, effort low, medium on long prompts) send only safe work to Haiku in live sessions? Settled by: No argument settles it, because the rubric has not yet run in a session that loaded it. Read the first week of simple-tier rows in ~/projects/data/logs/router/*.tsv and the weekly review, then read a sample of simple-tier transcripts in full; the result changes the Haiku share rule and nothing else.

nodes.label: Q2: Do outcome signals miss silent errors?
nodes.explain: The outcome labels (failed tools, rescued, redone, fixer started within 30 minutes) catch loud failure; how often does a Haiku or Sonnet run give a wrong answer none of them sees? Settled by: Argument settles the direction: absence of a retry is weak evidence, and the review already says so. Sampling traces is the only way to measure the rate, so lowering proposals carry 'read these traces' and a session samples before accepting.

nodes.label: Tier decision
nodes.explain: A proposed change to a tier rule with its evidence, the traces to read and a status; a session accepts or rejects it and records which. Source: docs/planning/evidence/router-weekly-review-sample.md:34. Code: /home/brian/code2/workspace/scripts/router_review.py:63.

nodes.label: Q5: Who applies a tier decision?
nodes.explain: When a session accepts a weekly decision (for example lower general-purpose from hard to standard), does it edit the tier rules directly and ship, or does a pull request wait for Brian? Recommendation: An agent session accepts or rejects each decision after reading the traces, ships the rule change through ship, and records the decision; Brian reads the weekly page only if he wants to. Default: Recommendation applies: the session that reads the weekly review decides and ships; nothing waits for Brian.

nodes.label: Q11: Is the classifier's cost measured?
nodes.explain: Is the classifier's cost ever measured? Settled by: Log query: the logs do not record classifications, so no per-call figure exists. The only measured number is the claude-haiku-5-5 row in the 2026-11-05 report ($0.03 main, $0.34 subagents, $0.37 in total), which mixes classifier and other Haiku use. The fix is to log each classification, then compute cost per call.
